correctness.rationale: For a,c>0, b≥0 and 1<p<∞, compute the unique norming functional of x∈ℓp² to obtain sup_{r≥0}[-a+br-cr^p]/[1+r^p]. The sign is that of br−a−cr^p. Its exact critical b is the global infimum a/r+cr^{p−1}, attained uniquely at r=[a/(c(p−1))]^{1/p}, giving βp=p a^{(p−1)/p} c^{1/p}/(p−1)^{(p−1)/p}. For p=1, the induced logarithmic matrix norm is max(−a,b−c); the complex phase maximizer has the same expression. Independent symbolic differentiation with SymPy yielded d(log βp)/dp=−p^{−2}log[(c/a)(p−1)] exactly, proving a unique maximum a+c at p=1+a/c, two transitions for max(a,c)<b<a+c, and the focal 1,9,10 single right-hand crossover. Constant-function vectors achieve the multiplication norm; semigroup logarithmic-norm inequality plus t↓0 derivative proves the optimal prefactor-one exponent −ωp. Finite p only; not a spectral-stability statement.
